opening_message:
Ticket 1: Belinda Fuentes (employee ID E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E039.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Admin is only allowed if the employee's role owns the system; Analyst does not own Payroll, so the maximum is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a contractor with basic security training per Security DB (note lists Analyst role). Contractors without advanced training max out at read, never admin. Admin requested exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: HR's note (authoritative for employment records) states Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a full-time Analyst. Per policy, full-time employees can have up to write; admin is only allowed if the employee's role owns the system, and Analyst does not own Payroll. The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (write), so the maximum is granted. Note: Security's note lists contractor status, but employment type is determined by HR records; even so, neither record supports admin, so the grant is capped at write under the fullest employee classification.
